report.summary: During the 3‑hour investigation window, checkout‑service’s resident memory increased 1.7× (from 721.79 MiB to 1225.50 MiB) and the service logged multiple OutOfMemoryError events and GC overhead limit warnings, indicating sustained heap pressure.

likely_causes.title: Memory leak in checkout‑service code
likely_causes.rationale: Repeated OutOfMemoryError events and GC overhead warnings, coupled with a sustained rise in resident memory, suggest that objects are not being released and are accumulating in the heap.

supporting_evidence.detail: process_resident_memory_bytes rose from 721.79 MiB to 1225.50 MiB
GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92%

likely_causes.title: Insufficient Java heap size configuration
likely_causes.rationale: The OOM errors and GC overhead warnings could also be caused by the JVM heap being too small for the workload.

supporting_evidence.detail: GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92%

next_steps: Collect and analyze heap dumps from the OOM timestamps to identify leaking objects.
Review recent code changes or deployments that could introduce memory retention.
Increase the JVM heap size (e.g., -Xmx) and monitor memory usage to confirm mitigation.
Implement continuous memory usage alerts to detect future regressions.
